_about: Hand-checked against Illumina/ExpansionHunter at 9f5db1d4ab72016b2d93330b9792842d71582622 (tag v5.0.0) on 2026-09-29, from README.md, docs/01_Introduction.md, docs/02_Installation.md, docs/03_Usage.md, docs/04_VariantCatalogFiles.md, variant_catalog/*/variant_catalog.json, example/run.sh, tools/, the v5.0.0 GitHub release and api.anaconda.org.

command.value: ExpansionHunter --reads <BAM/CRAM file with aligned reads> --reference <FASTA file with reference genome> --variant-catalog <JSON file specifying variants to genotype> --output-prefix <Prefix for the output files>

install.documented: Download the compiled binary of the latest release from GitHub releases, or build from source with CMake (mkdir build && cd build && cmake .. && make; binary at build/install/bin/ExpansionHunter; the build downloads abseil, boost, googletest, htslib and spdlog, so it needs internet).

extra_inputs.what: Variant catalog JSON (one LocusId / LocusStructure / ReferenceRegion / VariantType record per locus) for the loci to genotype, in the reference's contig naming. The repository ships variant_catalog/hg38/variant_catalog.json, but it holds 31 disease loci (AFF2 ... TCF4), none inside the 24 forensic windows of the STRhub slice.
extra_inputs.revised: 2026-09-29: STRhub now supplies an ExpansionHunter variant catalog of its panel loci (datasets/<type>/regions/eh_catalog.json, staged as /data/in/regions.json).

runnable_on_strhub_data.why: 2026-09-29: STRhub now supplies an ExpansionHunter variant catalog of its panel loci (datasets/<type>/regions/eh_catalog.json, staged as /data/in/regions.json). The documented command leaves the catalog to the user (`--variant-catalog <JSON file specifying variants to genotype>`, docs/03_Usage.md:15-18), as HipSTR leaves its regions BED; STRhub's catalog lists the 24 forensic loci the NA12878 slice covers.

was.why: --variant-catalog is a required parameter and STRhub supplies only BED layouts (HipSTR, GangSTR, STRsearch, BED4), no ExpansionHunter catalog. The catalog shipped in the repository covers 31 disease loci that all lie outside the +/-1 kb forensic windows of illumina-bam-hg38, so a run with it would genotype none of the dataset's loci. A catalog for the 24 panel loci would have to be written first; STRhub does not hold one.

notes: The README (README.md:26-29) only points to docs/; command, install and inputs are all in docs/01-04. Bioconda holds expansionhunter 5.0.0 but no document mentions it (available, not documented). tools/docker/debug/mallinfo2/Dockerfile is a developer debug build image ('Scripts and tooling related to ExpansionHunter development', tools/README.md:3), not an install route. The in-repo runnable example, example/run.sh:3-7, calls ../bin/ExpansionHunter on example/input/variants.bam, reference.fa and variants.json; ../bin is not where the documented CMake build puts the binary (build/install/bin/ExpansionHunter, docs/02_Installation.md:38-40). variant_catalog/ ships hg38 (chr-prefixed) and grch38 catalogs (31 disease loci) and hg19/grch37 ones (30); none contains a CODIS or other forensic locus. The default 'seeking' mode needs a sorted, indexed BAM (docs/03_Usage.md:46-50), which the dataset provides. Platform is inferred: the docs say PCR-free WGS short-read BAM/CRAM and reason in read and fragment lengths (docs/04_VariantCatalogFiles.md:74-78); they never name Illumina.
